blogs.title: How a 7B Open Model Got Close to GPT-4 at Math
blogs.description: A plain-English walkthrough of DeepSeekMath 7B’s headline results: 51.7% on the competition-level MATH benchmark without external tools or voting, and 60.9% with self-consistency over 64 samples. We’ll explain what these benchmarks mean, why they’re hard, and how a compact model closed much of the gap with closed systems like GPT-4 and Gemini Ultra.

blogs.title: From the Wild Web to a 120B-Token Math Corpus
blogs.description: Inside the data engine that powers DeepSeekMath: how the team mined Common Crawl with a fastText classifier, iteratively expanded sources, decontaminated benchmarks, and ended up with 120B high-quality math tokens. We’ll keep it non-technical while showing why data selection and multilingual coverage (not just English!) were crucial.

blogs.title: Why Coding Skills Make LLMs Better at Math
blogs.description: DeepSeekMath starts from a code-trained base and sees gains not just in coding but in general reasoning and math. We’ll unpack simple examples of how coding patterns map to logical structure, why program-of-thought helps, and what the experiments say about two-stage vs mixed training—and the surprise that arXiv-heavy training didn’t help much.

blogs.title: GRPO: PPO-Style Reinforcement Learning Without the Critic
blogs.description: Meet Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a lighter-weight alternative to PPO that skips the critic model and uses group-based baselines instead. We’ll explain how this cuts memory, why it aligns with how reward models compare answers, and how it pushed DeepSeekMath from 46.8% to 51.7% on MATH and 82.9% to 88.2% on GSM8K.

blogs.title: The Instruction-Tuning Cocktail: CoT, PoT, and Tool Use
blogs.description: How chain-of-thought, program-of-thought, and tool-integrated reasoning combine to make a strong math tutor. We’ll define each mode in friendly terms, show when to use Python tools, and break down how these ingredients helped DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B outperform larger open models across multiple benchmarks.

blogs.title: A Unified Map of SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO
blogs.description: All these training acronyms can be confusing. This guide puts them on one intuitive map—what data each uses, how they learn from feedback, and how they update the model. You’ll leave with a simple mental model to decide when to use supervised fine-tuning vs preference learning vs reinforcement learning.

blogs.title: Why RL Works Here: From ‘Sometimes Right’ to ‘Usually Right’
blogs.description: DeepSeekMath’s analysis suggests RL didn’t just make single attempts smarter—it made correct answers more reliably appear across samples (majority vote gains). We’ll explain Pass@K vs Maj@K in plain words, why distribution shaping matters for reasoning, and how this insight changes how we evaluate LLMs.

blogs.title: Multilingual Math: Building a Bilingual Problem Solver
blogs.description: Most math corpora are English-only; DeepSeekMath’s is not. This post shows how adding high-quality non-English data—especially Chinese—boosted math reasoning across languages. We’ll explore practical implications for global classrooms, content creators, and research communities.

blogs.title: From Classroom Solutions to Formal Proofs
blogs.description: Beyond word problems: DeepSeekMath also tackles formal math, turning informal statements into machine-checkable proofs in Isabelle. We’ll demystify autoformalization, explain why proof assistants matter for correctness, and show what the model’s miniF2F results signal for the future of verified math.

blogs.title: Build Your Own Domain LLM: Lessons You Can Reuse
blogs.description: A practical blueprint distilled from DeepSeekMath for teams targeting any specialized domain. We’ll cover data mining from Common Crawl, decontamination, why starting from a strong code model helps, when instruction tuning vs RL makes sense, and pitfalls like over-indexing on arXiv.
